body:
## Summary
The standing card the broadcast shows between explainers tells viewers which chat commands they can use. It is a hand copy of the Rust segment table, and it has already drifted. In SEG-02A it leaves out `!propose`, which the table allows, and it shows `!propose <scheme>` where the parser documents `<text>`. Derive the card from one committed artifact that a Rust test generates and gates for drift.

## Description
Today OnAir.tsx hard-codes five CommandRow constants and a per-segment switch (OnAir.tsx:43-58). The real vocabulary lives in `COMMAND_SPECS` (command.rs:21) and in each segment's `commands = [...]` (data/segments/*.toml). The daemon derives it for the console (catalog.rs:490), but the stage has no RPC and replays have no daemon, so it copied the data. This is the registry's `segment-as-state-table` failure mode 'the frozen view' (and 'prose duplicating the table'): an operator or viewer surface that projects the table and stops following it. The move follows `codegen` / drift-gating plus commit-vs-derive-policy. A new integration test in shadowrunr-segments renders `{segment -> [{name,args,what,rank_gated}]}` from `table::tables()` and `COMMAND_SPECS` in table order, with a `_generated` provenance key. It compares the result byte-for-byte with `apps/stage/src/generated/segment-commands.json`, and `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites the file. footage.rs:613 sets the precedent for a Rust test reading a stage file. `standingCommands` then reads the JSON. The stage keeps exactly one presentation rule of its own: `!vote` shows only while a poll is open. The stage stays offline-capable, because the JSON is bundled, and drift becomes a red `cargo test` instead of a wrong card on air.

## Flow
- write the golden test first (fails: file absent)
- generate the JSON with UPDATE_GOLDEN=1; commit
- write onair.test.ts cases for SEG-02A !propose and the args (fail against the hand list)
- replace the CommandRow constants and switch with a lookup over the JSON, keeping the vote-while-poll rule
- DESIGN.md: replace 'copied' with 'generated + gated by cargo test'

## Expected impact
Viewers in SEG-02A learn that they can propose schemes, and every command row matches what the parser accepts. A future command, argument change or segment edit cannot reach air with a stale card, because CI fails first. This also removes the stage's last hand copy of daemon rules from OnAir.

## Evaluation
Claim: the on-air standing card equals the segment table for every segment.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no golden file or test, SEG-02A omits !propose, args differ)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: architecture (a new cross-language generated artifact; no contract or schema change)
evidence: apps/stage/src/OnAir.tsx:43 `const PROPOSE: CommandRow = { cmd: "!propose", args: "<scheme>", what: "Propose a scheme. Rank-gated." };` | OnAir.tsx:54-55 `case "SEG-02A": return [HINT, GRADE];` | command.rs:41-44 `name: "propose", args: "<text>", what: "Propose a scheme. Rank-gated.", rank_gated: true` | seg-02a.toml:24 `commands = ["hint", "grade", "propose", "vote"]` | grep COMMAND_SPECS: only command.rs, daemon/catalog.rs, console testgen.ts (a test fixture copy), stage OnAir.tsx comment

critic.reason: Floor failure: a real but S-sized fix (two-line drift plus a golden test) dressed up as M; route it as a quick fix instead.

title: Live preview cannot look back: a keyframed DVR window over the live ring
acceptance: LiveStore fed 3000 contiguous seq events (ring 2000); store.sceneAt(ts of event #2500) -> deep-equals new Timeline(all 3000).advanceTo(that ts)
store.sceneAt(head ts) -> the same object as store.scene (the live head is never re-folded)
any seek inside the held window -> store.lastSeekFolds <= KEYFRAME_EVERY (100), never a fold from the window start
store.sceneAt(t older than the oldest held keyframe) -> { clamped: true } and the earliest reachable scene, never a wrong partial fold
a new run_id or a stream_start -> keyframes cleared; sceneAt(a ts from the old run) -> clamped to the new run's start

dvr transport: follow --seek(t)--> behind(t); play advances at speed and returns to follow on reaching the head; goLive -> follow; in behind, voiceCaption is not used (estimated captions for the past moment)
broadcast=1 -> no DVR state exists and the canvas always draws the head (unchanged OBS path)

apps/stage/src/App.tsx:95,144 - ...but live has no Timeline, so seek() returns at `if (!timeline) return;`: an on-screen marker that does nothing

body:
## Summary
During a live run, an operator watching the stage preview who misses a moment (a redaction flash, a decree, a vote result) cannot look back until the run ends. The scrubber, play and speed controls are disabled, and the clip markers drawn on the track are inert buttons. The last 2000 events are already in memory. Add a DVR window: scrub back inside the held window in the preview only, play from there at speed, then go back to live.

## Description
This applies registry `time-travel-replay` / scrub-performance: keyframes every N items, so a seek restores the nearest keyframe at or before t and re-folds only the tail. Worst-case seek cost is then bounded by the keyframe spacing, not the stream length. `transport-and-time-mapping` governs the follow/behind states. `LiveStore` records `{ringIndex, ts, scene}` every 100 applied events. A keyframe is only a retained reference, because `reduce` spreads prev. Keyframes are evicted with the ring, so memory stays bounded at about 20 scenes. `sceneAt(t)` picks the newest keyframe still inside the ring with ts <= t, folds the ring tail to t, and reports `clamped` when t falls before the window. Per the law, the fold is never authoritative over the head: at the head it returns `store.scene` itself. A pure `dvr.ts` transport (`follow | behind{t, playing}`) owns the preview clock. App and Controls enable the scrubber over `[windowStart, head]`, show 'N s behind live' and a GO LIVE button, and make clip markers seek. While behind, captions use the estimated timing, because the voice is live audio. The broadcast view (`?broadcast=1`, which sandbox and recording use) never builds DVR state, and acks keep reading lastSeq, so the OBS path and the stage_ack gate do not change.

## Flow
- dvr.test.ts and live.test.ts cases first (all fail: no sceneAt, no transport)
- LiveStore: keyframes aligned to the ring, sceneAt, clear on reset
- dvr.ts: pure transport reducer
- App: in live non-broadcast, scene = follow ? store.scene : store.sceneAt(t); Controls: enable track/markers/play in live, add a behind-live badge and GO LIVE
- DESIGN.md Live mode: the DVR window and its limits

## Expected impact
The operator gets a 'wait, go back' over the held window of a live run, the live clip markers start working, and keyboard seek works in live. All of this stays off the broadcast path and leaves the acks unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: a live preview can be scrubbed inside the held window, with exact scenes and a bounded fold cost, without touching broadcast or acks.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no sceneAt, no keyframes, live seek is a no-op)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: none (stage-local, additive)
evidence: Controls.tsx:94 `if (!el || live) return;` | Controls.tsx:110 `disabled={live} title="Space"` | Controls.tsx:147 `onSeek(Math.max(start, m.at - 3000));` | App.tsx:95 `new Timeline(...)` only when `loaded && !live` | App.tsx:144 `if (!timeline) return;` | live.ts:12 `export const RING_MAX = 2000;` | playback.ts:37-39 `if (t < this.appliedTo) { this.cursor = 0; this.state = initialScene(); }`

critic.reason: Ambitious, well-bounded, and the core cases would catch a wrong fold.
